channel.title: OAM reference: contributor notes :: Go Kure — Launcher
channel.description: Each page here belongs to one part of the OAM and component reference (api-reference/oam and api-reference/oam-components). It holds what a contributor needs and a reader of the reference does not: the code that implements an entry, the issues behind it, and the tests that hold its claims. A page is named after its reference part and has one section per entry, with up to three lists: Implementation: the helper or file that builds the entry. History: the issues that introduced or changed it. Tests: the tests that hold a claim of the reference, with the claim each one holds. Text on these pages is moved from the reference without rewording. A claim stays in the reference; its test or issue reference moves here.

item.title: Kinds: MetalLB
item.description: Implementation, history and tests of the entries on the reference page Kinds: MetalLB. Every test named here is in pkg/oam/builtin/components/metallb_kinds_internal_test.go unless a line says another file. metallb-bfdprofile Implementation: built on policyFreeKind as the kinds above are, and emits that one object. History: go-kure/launcher#790 (the kind-named projection); go-kure/launcher#922 (the object kind policy, oam.ObjectKindPolicy). Tests: TestMetalLBKinds_NoDefaultIsLost fails on a default a dependency bump adds to a field that could not carry an authored empty value. TestMetalLBKinds_RequiredMatchCRD holds that to the linked module’s v1beta1 CRD (“that” is the reference’s “Required: nothing”). The CRD declares none; TestMetalLBKinds_ExpressionRules fails on one that is added (“none” is the CRD’s expression rules). metallb-bgpadvertisement Implementation: built on policyFreeKind as the two kinds above are, and emits that one object. History: go-kure/launcher#790 (the kind-named projection); go-kure/launcher#883 (the Required list is generated from the linked module’s v1beta1 CRD); go-kure/launcher#922 (the object kind policy). Tests: TestMetalLBKinds_NoDefaultIsLost holds the defaults of the linked CRD to that (“that” is the reference’s account of the two aggregation lengths: pointers, whose API defaults are 32 and 128, one route per address). TestMetalLBKinds_RequiredMatchCRD holds it to that CRD as well (“it” is the Required list, generated from the linked module’s v1beta1 CRD). TestMetalLBKinds_ExpressionRules holds the kind’s answer to the API server’s for the linked CRD, on properties that break the rule and on properties that keep it, and fails on a rule that is added or reworded. metallb-bgppeer Implementation: built on policyHeldKind, the helper of the kinds above with one check under the environment policy, and emits that one object. The version it is built at, and why, are in the reference. History: go-kure/launcher#790 (the kind-named projection); go-kure/launcher#883 (the Required list is generated from the linked module’s v1beta2 CRD); go-kure/launcher#922 (the object kind policy). Tests: TestMetalLBKinds_EmitTheServedVersion holds each kind to the version its CRD serves and stores. TestMetalLBKinds_NoDefaultIsLost holds the kind’s list of such fields to the linked CRD (“such fields” are the reference’s fields with a default the type cannot carry, as peerPort). TestMetalLBKinds_RequiredMatchCRD holds it to that CRD as well (“it” is the Required list, generated from the linked module’s v1beta2 CRD). TestMetalLBKinds_ExpressionRules holds the kind’s answer to the API server’s for the linked CRD, on properties that break each rule and on properties that keep it, and fails on a rule that is added or reworded. TestMetalLBBGPPeerKind_SessionPassword holds this (“this” is the reference’s account of password under each policy; the test is in metallb_bgppeer_test.go). metallb-community Implementation: built on policyFreeKind as the kinds above are, and emits that one object. History: go-kure/launcher#790 (the kind-named projection); go-kure/launcher#922 (the object kind policy). Tests: TestMetalLBKinds_NoDefaultIsLost fails on a default a dependency bump adds to a field that could not carry an authored empty value. TestMetalLBKinds_RequiredMatchCRD holds that to the linked module’s v1beta1 CRD (“that” is the reference’s “Required: nothing”). The CRD declares none; TestMetalLBKinds_ExpressionRules fails on one that is added (“none” is the CRD’s expression rules). metallb-ipaddresspool Implementation: built on policyFreeKind, and emits that one object. The type name carries the metallb- prefix as the kinds of Cilium’s API carry theirs: both APIs have a pool of addresses and an advertisement for BGP. History: go-kure/launcher#790 (the kind-named projection); go-kure/launcher#883 (the Required list is generated from the fields the linked module’s v1beta1 CRD requires and the type writes unauthored); go-kure/launcher#922 (the object kind policy). Tests: TestMetalLBKinds_NoDefaultIsLost holds the defaults of the linked CRD to that: one that is not the field’s empty value, on a field that is no pointer, fails there (“that” is the reference’s account of autoAssign and avoidBuggyIPs). …so a dependency bump that adds, drops or moves one fails until it is regenerated; TestMetalLBKinds_RequiredMatchCRD holds it to that CRD as well (“one” is a required field, and “it” is the Required list, generated from the fields the linked module’s v1beta1 CRD requires and the type writes unauthored). The CRD declares none; TestMetalLBKinds_ExpressionRules fails on one that is added (“none” is the CRD’s expression rules). metallb-l2advertisement Implementation: built on policyFreeKind as metallb-ipaddresspool is, and emits that one object. History: go-kure/launcher#790 (the kind-named projection); go-kure/launcher#883 (the Required list is generated from the linked module’s v1beta1 CRD); go-kure/launcher#922 (the object kind policy). Tests: TestMetalLBKinds_RequiredMatchCRD holds it to that CRD as well (“it” is the Required list, generated from the linked module’s v1beta1 CRD). The CRD declares none; TestMetalLBKinds_ExpressionRules fails on one that is added (“none” is the CRD’s expression rules).

item.title: The null contract and two spellings of one field
item.description: Implementation, history and tests of the sections on the reference page The null contract and two spellings of one field. Text in square brackets is added here to say what a moved sentence refers to. The null contract Implementation: authoredValue — the presence primitive parseStringField, parseObjectField, parseInt32Field, parseInt64Field, parseObjectList and parseStringList all go through — does exactly that, so calling any of them directly already complies. They classify a typed nil as null too — map[string]any(nil) or []any(nil) inside an any, which is what a lowering rule assembled in Go produces for an unset optional and is not == nil. [“that” is the reference’s “read a null under an optional property as omission”; “They” are the six helpers named in this sentence.] A new optional field is read with the helper for its type instead: parseStringField (or requiredStringField when the field is required), parseBoolField, parseInt32Field, parseInt64Field, parseObjectField, parseObjectList or parseStringList. Each already reads an explicit null as absence through authoredValue, so a wrapper would only repeat that check. [“instead” is instead of an optional* wrapper; “a wrapper” is one of those, listed under History.] History: It is written down because “null” has several readers — the emission validator’s requiredness check and its optional-key strip, its array-element guard, enforcePlatformReserved, this package’s parsers, and the Kubernetes API itself — and each was aligned separately, so each round of review found the reader the last round had not touched. [“It” is the reference’s rule on the null contract.] This used to require a separate optional* wrapper family (optionalString, optionalObject, optionalInt32, optionalInt64, optionalObjectList, optionalStringList) layered in front of the plain parsers. go-kure/launcher#394 moved the handling into the shared helpers themselves, which made every wrapper an exact no-op forward; they were removed and every caller now uses the parse* helper directly. go-kure/launcher#423, go-kure/launcher#394 and go-kure/launcher#570 converted the parsers they covered; the last of them are listed with the null row of the deployment table above. [“the parsers they covered” are the parsers that answer presence with a bare v, ok := props[key], the first limit of the reference; “the deployment table above” is on the reference page of the deployment kind.] Both limits met on one key, and it was the second row of that table. namespaceSelector is parsed twice in this repository: here, for pod affinity, through parseSchedulingSelector (parseObjectField), where any null is omission — which upstream reads as “this pod’s namespace”; and in the networkpolicy trait, through parseNPPeer. A typed nil used to satisfy the networkpolicy trait’s own type assertion and yield an empty selector — all namespaces, the widest possible answer — while an untyped nil already read as omission there, so one input landed on opposite ends of the range depending on which Go nil shape produced it. Both parsers now route their presence check through oam.IsNullValue’s reflect-based classification, which treats a typed nil the same as an untyped one, so the two halves converge: a null namespaceSelector, however it was constructed, is omission on both paths. [“Both limits” are the two limits the reference lists; “that table” is its labelSelector and namespaceSelector table; “here” is the handler parsers.] The same typed-nil shape reached list elements. parseObjectList read a null key as absence, but a typed-nil element ([]any{map[string]any(nil)}) passed its per-element assertion as an empty object, where an untyped null element is refused (tolerations[0]: must be an object, got <nil>). Most callers then failed on a missing required field anyway. tolerations did not: an empty entry became an Exists toleration with no key, which tolerates every taint. The element is now normalised to a null first, so every caller refuses both shapes identically (go-kure/launcher#465). The list readers that do not go through parseObjectList (envFrom, httpHeaders, volumes, volumeMounts, sidecar ports, the Job successPolicy/podFailurePolicy rules and onPodConditions, volumeClaimTemplates, valuesFrom, scopeOverrides) pass each element through nullElem first, for the same untyped refusal and message. [“The same typed-nil shape” is the one of the entry above.] Tests: TestNoOptionalFieldWrappers (no_optional_wrappers_internal_test.go) keeps them removed: it fails on any function or method whose name starts with optional. It parses every production .go file directly in this package’s directory — every file, not only common.go, and never a _test.go file or a subdirectory — and fails if it parsed none, so a wrong working directory cannot pass it vacuously. [“them” are the optional* wrappers of the History entry above.] Fixed as go-kure/launcher#430; networkpolicy_internal_test.go’s TestParseNPPeer_NamespaceSelectorPresenceCases pins the typed-nil case directly. [“Fixed” is the namespaceSelector split of the History entry that starts “Both limits”.] Two spellings of one field Implementation: foldedKey [the helper behind the reference’s sentence on the helmrelease verify check that still refuses a pair in which one spelling is null, which the decode lets through]. History: Before, those documents built. [“those documents” are the ones a kind that decodes by itself builds, listed in the reference’s gitrepository and helmrelease sentence.]
